packageRules.description: Non-major Action bumps: Renovate opens the PR, merging stays with .github/workflows/automerge.yml via the automerge label (PAT path keeps the lovable->dev MERGE / others SQUASH policy). The 7-day wait binds here even though scripts/check-dep-release-age.mjs cannot see it - that gate diffs package-lock, which has no workflow pins.
Major Action bumps need a human decision.
npm: only direct devDependencies may reach the automerge label - this is the equivalent of the dependency-type:direct:development condition dependabot-auto-triage.yml used to apply.
npm majors are human-decided, devDependencies included.

AAV-1301's eslint ceiling. The old Dependabot ignore covered @eslint/js >= 10 because that bump turned dev's peer-dep-check and lint red twice, and the ceiling moved here when dependabot.yml went away - but it only pinned @eslint/js while `eslint` itself stayed uncapped, which is half a ceiling: the pair must move together. Measured 2026-10-09 peer ranges: eslint-plugin-import allows up to ^9 (NO ^10 -> strict npm ci fails, and peer-dep-check is required on dev AND main), while eslint-plugin-react-hooks ^7 and typescript-eslint ^8 already allow ^10. So the blocker is eslint-plugin-import; 9.x minor/patch keep flowing, and scripts/renovate-config.test.mjs pins this range set so the ceiling cannot silently cover one package again.

vitest and @vitest/* are one peer-locked family: each @vitest package's peerDependencies pin vitest to the exact same version, so bumping one alone fails the strict `npm ci` that ci.yml's peer-dep-check runs (required on dev AND main). Dependabot's #731 did exactly that - it raised vitest to 5.0.3 while @vitest/coverage-v8 stayed on ^4.1.11 - and could never merge, which is why the family must be reviewed together (same reasoning as the node runtime rule).
Runtime dependencies never carry the automerge label: they ship to users.
Dev Container image/features: human-reviewed because the typescript-node tag must stay aligned with the node-version used by CI workflows.

Node lives in two places here - the workflow node-version (node datasource) and the Dev Container image tag (docker datasource). Nothing but a shared release makes them agree, so group them: a bump must move both or neither, otherwise CI runs a Node the Codespaces image does not have. Always human-reviewed.
